info.title: Orgo API
info.description: Launch cloud computers that AI agents can control and interact with. Create workspaces, provision computers, and control them programmatically.

tags.name: Computer Actions
tags.description: Control mouse, keyboard, and execute commands

tags.name: Templates
tags.description: Author, build, and launch reproducible computers from templates

get.description: Returns the canonical orgo.ai/v1 template schema as JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) - every field, its type, accepted values, and a description. Public endpoint: no API key required, permissive CORS, cacheable.
Lists the templates published under your account.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.description: Filter to a single namespace. Your own templates default to `default`.

post.description: Publishes a template document (YAML or JSON) to your registry. Requires a Scale plan. Refs are immutable: re-publishing the same `namespace/name@version` with different content returns 409 unless `force=true`.

parameters.name: auto_build
parameters.description: Build the golden snapshot immediately after publishing.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Overwrite an existing version in place (delete + republish). Useful while iterating on one version number.

schema.description: The orgo.ai/v1 template document as YAML.

403.description: Publishing requires a Scale plan or higher

409.description: A different template is already published at this ref. Bump the version or use force=true.

post.description: Validates a template document against the orgo.ai/v1 schema without storing anything. No side effects - safe to call on every keystroke in an editor.

get.description: Lists the curated templates Orgo publishes and maintains (the `system` namespace), e.g. `system/claude-code@1.0.0`. Launchable on any paid plan.
Lists every published version of one curated template.
Lists every published version of one template you own.
Fetches one template version, including the full document. Use the `system` namespace for curated templates, e.g. `system/claude-code/1.0.0`.

delete.description: Deletes one published version you own. Running computers already launched from it are unaffected. Curated templates cannot be deleted.

post.description: Kicks off an asynchronous golden-snapshot build and returns immediately. Requires a Scale plan. If an identical digest is already built, returns the existing golden with reused=true.

403.description: Building requires a Scale plan or higher

429.description: Build rate limit or host capacity reached. Back off and retry.

get.description: Returns the current build state of a version. Poll until status is `ready`.

delete.description: Cancels an in-flight golden build. Returns 404 if no build is running.

get.description: Server-Sent Events stream of live golden-build progress. Each `data:` frame is a BuildEvent JSON object. The stream ends after a terminal `ready` (or error) event.

post.description: Boots a short-lived, auto-reaped preview computer from a template ref - the in-editor test run. Requires a Scale plan. For a persistent computer, use POST /computers with template_ref instead.

403.description: Test-runs require a Scale plan or higher

409.description: The template's build is not ready

429.description: Run-VM rate limit or concurrency cap reached

delete.description: Stops a preview computer booted from POST /templates/run.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The preview computer's desktop id (the `desktop_id` from the run response).

get.description: Lists every workspace you own or belong to, each with its computers embedded. For backwards compatibility the same array is also returned under a deprecated `projects` key; new clients should read `workspaces`.

workspaces.description: Workspaces you own or belong to, each with its computers embedded.

post.description: Creates a new workspace. Workspace names must be unique per user.

name.description: Workspace name. Must be unique within your account.

400.description: Workspace name already exists or invalid

get.description: Returns a workspace by ID, including its computers.

post.description: Creates a new virtual computer in a workspace. The computer starts automatically after creation.

get.description: Returns computer details including current status.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a computer and all its data.

post.description: Starts a stopped computer. The disk is restored and the computer cold-boots on a freshly chosen host with a new IP address; in-memory state is not restored.
Stops a running computer. The disk is preserved and no compute is charged while stopped; the host is released. Start boots it fresh on a new host (new IP).
Restarts a computer. Equivalent to stop + start.
Creates a copy of a computer with the same disk state. Counts toward your plan's computer limit.

patch.description: Live-resizes a running computer's CPU, RAM, disk, or bandwidth. All fields optional — only include what you want to change.

vcpus.description: New CPU count. Capped by plan.

mem_gb.description: New RAM in GB. Live resize is capped at 32 GB (the VMM boot-memory ceiling); larger sizes are only available at create time. Also capped by your plan.

disk_size_gb.description: New disk size in GB. Grow only — shrinking not supported.

bandwidth_limit_mbps.description: New bandwidth cap in Mbps. Capped by plan.

patch.description: Moves a computer to a different workspace. Both source and destination must be owned by you.

project_id.description: Deprecated alias for `workspace_id`. Accepted on input for backwards compatibility.

get.description: Returns the VNC password for direct VNC connection to the computer. Only accessible by workspace owners and members.

403.description: Access denied - not a workspace owner or member

get.description: Captures a screenshot of the computer display and returns a URL to the stored image.

image.description: URL of the captured image, usually a path relative to the API origin. Fetch it to get the bytes.

post.description: Performs a mouse click at the specified coordinates.
Performs a mouse drag from start to end coordinates.
Types text on the computer keyboard.
Presses a key or key combination (e.g., Enter, Tab, ctrl+c).
Scrolls the mouse wheel up or down.
Pauses execution for the specified duration.
Executes a bash command on the computer.

example.output:
total 32
drwxr-xr-x 4 user user 4096 Jan 15 10:30 .
drwxr-xr-x 3 root root 4096 Jan 15 10:00 ..
-rw-r--r-- 1 user user  220 Jan 15 10:00 .bashrc
drwxr-xr-x 2 user user 4096 Jan 15 10:30 Desktop

post.description: Executes Python code on the computer.
Uploads a file to a workspace. Maximum file size is 10MB.

desktopId.description: Optional computer ID to associate the file with

get.description: Lists all files in a workspace, optionally filtered by computer.

parameters.name: desktopId
parameters.description: Optional computer ID to filter by

post.description: Exports a file from the computer's filesystem and returns a download URL.

400.description: Computer not running or invalid path

get.description: Returns a signed download URL for a file. URLs expire in 1 hour.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a file from storage.

post.description: Permanently deletes a workspace and every computer, file and member record in it.

Template.description: An orgo.ai/v1 template document. Only `api_version` and `template` are required. See the full JSON Schema at GET /template-schema, or the schema guide at https://docs.orgo.ai/guides/templates/schema.

digest.description: Content-addressed SHA-256 digest of the canonical template. Two semantically identical templates always share a digest.

auto_build.description: Present only with ?auto_build=true. The kicked-off build's status, e.g. "building".

build_time_ms.description: Build duration in milliseconds. Present when ready.

reused.description: Whether an existing golden with the same digest was reused.

error.description: Failure reason. Present when status is failed.

BuildEvent.description: One frame of the build-events SSE stream.

source.description: Origin of the line, e.g. apt, pip, npm, builder.

line.description: A single line of build output.

field.description: Dotted path to the offending field.

TemplateRunResponse.description: A short-lived preview computer booted from a template ref. Connect to it like any computer; it is auto-reaped.

desktop_id.description: Ephemeral desktop id. Use it for same-origin connection URLs and to stop the run via DELETE /templates/run?id=.

instance_id.description: Stable identifier for the underlying compute instance. Use this for proxy hostnames and for any client that needs to reference the VM across restarts.

hostname.description: Same-origin host for the computer's connection endpoints (always `www.orgo.ai`).

connection_url.description: Same-origin connection base (https://www.orgo.ai/desktops/{instance_id}). Append /ws/websockify, /ws/terminal, or /ws/audio for WebSocket endpoints; HTTP Desktop API calls go to https://www.orgo.ai/api/desktops/{instance_id}/proxy/{endpoint}.

vnc_password.description: VNC / WebSocket Bearer token. Rotates on every restart - do not persist across restarts.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace to create the computer in

ram.description: RAM in GB. Capped by plan.

disk_size_gb.description: Disk size in GB. Capped by plan.

template_ref.description: Launch from a template's golden snapshot instead of a base image. Format `namespace/name@version`, e.g. `system/claude-code@1.0.0` (curated) or `default/my-template@1.0.0` (your own). The hardware fields above override the template's defaults. The template's build must be `ready`.

key.description: Key or key combination (e.g., Enter, Tab, ctrl+c, alt+F4)

seconds.description: How long to pause, in seconds

duration.description: Deprecated alias for `seconds`. Accepted on input for backwards compatibility.

connection_name.description: Name of the configured RTMP connection

path.description: Path to file on computer (e.g., Desktop/results.txt)

Forbidden.description: Access denied or plan limit reached

bearerAuth.description: API key authentication. Get your key at orgo.ai/workspaces
